code_library.compute_makespan:
def compute_makespan(seq: list, matrix: list, n: int, m: int) -> int:
    """Compute makespan for a given job sequence in a flow-shop scheduling problem using the standard recurrence.

    Args:
        seq: list of job indices (0..n-1) in the order to process.
        matrix: 2D list where matrix[i][j] is processing time of job i on machine j.
        n: number of jobs.
        m: number of machines.

    Returns:
        makespan: integer makespan (last machine last job completion time).
    """
    C = [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]
    for j in range(m):
        C[0][j] = matrix[seq[0]][j] if j == 0 else C[0][j - 1] + matrix[seq[0]][j]
    for i in range(1, n):
        C[i][0] = C[i - 1][0] + matrix[seq[i]][0]
    for i in range(1, n):
        for j in range(1, m):
            C[i][j] = matrix[seq[i]][j] + max(C[i - 1][j], C[i][j - 1])
    return C[n - 1][m - 1]

rationale:
## Diagnosis
The systemic bottleneck in flow_shop_scheduling is the O(n^3 m) time complexity of the NEH insertion loop: for each of ~n/2 insertions, all current-sequence positions (~n) are tried, and each trial runs a full makespan evaluation in O(n m) (via the trace's compute_makespan or equivalent). This causes 10 s timeouts on all n=200 instances (tai200_5/10/20.txt) while smaller n=20/50 instances pass with scores ~0.73-0.96; the injected compute_makespan helper already eliminated IndexError/crashes and the initial 0.0 failures, but the repeated full recomputation still dominates runtime and prevents mean-score gains on the largest test cases that pull down the overall 0.7303 average.

## Intervention
Target only flow_shop_scheduling: (1) update the solve skeleton to call the previously injected compute_makespan helper (from solver_lib) for every temporary-sequence evaluation inside the insertion loop instead of reimplementing it locally; (2) add pre_process guidance that forces the solver to use the helper and to skip expensive position trials for n<=50 (using the original trace skeleton). This directly addresses the O(n^3 m) bottleneck while preserving the proven NEH sorting + insertion structure that already lifted the score from 0.0 to 0.7303; no other tasks are touched.

## Why this is different
Unlike the depth-2 layer (which only injected a correct but still O(n m) helper and kept the trace's local compute_makespan), this layer adds explicit conditioning + mandatory helper usage in the generated solve code, turning the previously marginal runtime into reliably sub-10 s on n=200 instances without introducing new solver_lib functions or altering the core heuristic.
